findings.claim: Drive aicore/updater is an exact eight-file alias of the frozen Project-Frankenstein updater subtree, including frank_updater.py and frank_recovery.py. It should be provenance-linked and deduplicated rather than treated as independent implementation evidence.
Updater preflight has no dirty-worktree preservation gate, while rollback executes `git reset --hard` to the saved SHA. A rollback can therefore erase unrelated tracked local edits.
Update lock reclamation uses mtime >600s and unlinks the lock without validating the stored PID/process liveness. A legitimate long-running update can therefore lose exclusion to a second updater.
Failed affected-service stops are warnings and do not block the update transaction, so source/dependency mutation can proceed without proving all required stateful writers are quiescent.

Rollback restores only Git source state plus service starts. Because pip dependency synchronization happens inside the rollback-gated region but is not reversed, a later failure can leave old source with new dependencies. The historical transaction is not version-atomic across source and runtime package state.

Service start failures are warnings; health check records failure but returns True; main run ignores start/health/model readiness results and still prints UPDATE COMPLETE. A degraded runtime can therefore receive a success outcome.
Post-update overlay repair can mutate the installed systemd user service outside the Git repository after the rollback-gated steps, without an inverse receipt bound to the update transaction.
Database recovery continues to backup, wipe and reference-copy after individual service stop failures; it does not prove all authoritative DB writers are quiescent before destructive replacement.

Recovery performs no post-copy SQLite integrity/schema/version compatibility gate and returns Recovery Complete even when one or more service starts fail. Recovery success is therefore not equivalent to restored semantic readiness.

current_architecture_implications.harness: Add all nine updater/recovery oracles as mandatory differential tests for H1/H2/H3 and the final Recovery receipt.
current_architecture_implications.claycode: Model update/recovery as typed multi-resource transactions with explicit commit/abort/effect/inverse semantics; Git SHA alone is not transaction identity.
current_architecture_implications.unifieddb: Require writer quiescence/lease release plus DB version/schema/integrity receipts around recovery; data restoration and runtime readiness are distinct gates.
current_architecture_implications.frank: A successful update/recovery must mean semantic readiness, not merely source checkout or process start.
current_architecture_implications.clay: Use the historical failure family as direct evidence for Safe-Effect geometry: authority/effect scope must include source, dependencies, machine config, models, DBs and runtime readiness together.

earned_work_candidate.mechanism_or_result: Exact historical updater/recovery implementation plus nine code-derived fail-open/mixed-version/destructive-recovery oracles eliminate rediscovery and define concrete recovery acceptance tests.
earned_work_candidate.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: H1/H2/H3/final recovery harness must instantiate these failure conditions and show the current mediated transaction either fails closed or restores the complete resource-version set before success.
